youtube.aciklama:
Vestibular tests measure labyrinth function, but they do not show how much dizziness affects a person's life. In this lesson we cover the structure, scoring and interpretation of the Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI), the idea of meaningful change, the Activities-specific Balance Confidence scale (ABC), and how to use these scales in the clinical workflow.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: Jacobson and Newman, The development of the Dizziness Handicap Inventory, Arch Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg (1990); Whitney et al., Is perception of handicap related to functional performance in persons with vestibular dysfunction?, Otol Neurotol (2004); Powell and Myers, The Activities-specific Balance Confidence (ABC) Scale, J Gerontol (1995); Jacobson and Calder, A screening version of the Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI-S), Am J Otol (1998); Lajoie and Gallagher, Predicting falls within the elderly community, Arch Gerontol Geriatr (2004); Karapolat et al., Turkish DHI validity study, J Int Adv Otol (2009); Canbal et al., Turkish DHI validity and reliability study (2016); Karapolat et al., Turkish ABC scale, Int J Rehabil Res (2010); Ayhan et al., Turkish ABC scale, Turkish Journal of Geriatrics (2014); Jacobson and Shepard, Balance Function Assessment and Management.

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson we will learn about self-report scales that measure how dizziness affects daily life.
We will cover in detail the most widely used scale, the Dizziness Handicap Inventory, and the Activities-specific Balance Confidence scale.

maddeler.metin: A scale puts impact into numbers

cumleler: Vestibular tests measure the function of the labyrinth and reflex pathways, but they do not show what the person experiences in daily life.
Of two people with a similar caloric weakness, one may return to work while the other struggles to leave the house.
Self-report scales record the impact of symptoms on life from the person's own point of view, in numbers.
These scales do not make a diagnosis, but they help with treatment planning, goal setting and follow-up.
They are also the tools most often used to show the outcome of rehabilitation.
Choose versions validated in the patient's language; in Türkiye, validated Turkish adaptations of these scales are available.

cumleler.yazi: The Dizziness Handicap Inventory, or DHI, was developed by Jacobson and Newman in 1990.
cumleler.ses: The Dizziness Handicap Inventory, or D H I, was developed by Jacobson and Newman in nineteen ninety.

cumleler: The scale has 25 items, grouped into three subscales.
The physical subscale has 7 items; for example, it asks whether moving the head quickly or bending over makes symptoms worse.
The functional subscale has 9 items about the impact on daily tasks such as work, housework, social activities and getting around alone.
The emotional subscale has 9 items about embarrassment, anxiety, feeling handicapped and the impact on relationships.
The physical subscale scores up to 28, and the other two up to 36 each.
So the total score ranges from 0 to 100.
For each item, the person chooses one of three answers.
A yes answer scores 4, sometimes scores 2, and no scores 0.
The points are added; the higher the total, the greater the impact of dizziness on daily life.
The person should complete the scale themselves; the clinician does not steer the answers, only explains wording that is unclear.
For people with reading difficulty or vision problems, the items can be read aloud in a neutral tone.
Because there are few answer options, the scale is quick to fill in; most people finish in a few minutes.
In the grading of Whitney and colleagues, 0 to 30 points is mild, 31 to 60 moderate, and 61 to 100 severe handicap.
Some sources instead use 16 to 34 as mild, 36 to 52 as moderate, and 54 or more as severe, so the grading is only a guide.
In follow-up, what matters most is how the score changes over time in the same person.
Based on Jacobson and Newman's data, a difference of about 18 points is needed for a change to count as beyond measurement error.
In this example, the score is 58 before rehabilitation and falls to 34 afterward.
This drop of twenty four points points to a change beyond measurement error.
Subscale scores are also looked at separately; for example, a high emotional score may suggest that anxiety is in the foreground.

maddeler.metin: Caloric weakness does not predict handicap

cumleler.yazi: In most studies, the link between DHI scores and vestibular test results is weak to moderate.
cumleler.ses: In most studies, the link between D H I scores and vestibular test results is weak to moderate.

cumleler: For example, the size of a caloric weakness does not on its own predict how much handicap the person feels.
So the scale is used alongside the tests, not instead of them.

cumleler.yazi: The DHI does not show the cause either; benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, Meniere's or vestibular migraine can give similar scores.
cumleler.ses: The D H I does not show the cause either; benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, Meniere's or vestibular migraine can give similar scores.

cumleler: A high score, especially on the emotional subscale, is a reminder to also ask about anxiety and persistent dizziness.
The result is shared with the patient, and rehabilitation goals are discussed together.

cumleler.yazi: In Türkiye, a Turkish adaptation of the DHI and studies of its validity and reliability have been published.
cumleler.ses: In Türkiye, a Turkish adaptation of the D H I and studies of its validity and reliability have been published.

cumleler: A study in people with unilateral peripheral vestibular disease found high internal consistency and responsiveness to change.
The same study found relatively low test-retest reliability; later Turkish validation studies add to this information.

cumleler.yazi: The DHI also has a ten-item screening version, known as the DHI-S.
cumleler.ses: The D H I also has a ten-item screening version, known as the D H I S.

cumleler: The short form suits quick screening; for detailed follow-up, the 25-item form is usually preferred.

cumleler.yazi: The Activities-specific Balance Confidence scale, or ABC, was developed by Powell and Myers in 1995.
cumleler.ses: The Activities-specific Balance Confidence scale, or ABC, was developed by Powell and Myers in nineteen ninety five.

cumleler: The scale asks how confident the person is that they will not lose their balance while doing daily activities.
There are sixteen activities, such as walking around the house, going downstairs, standing on a chair, or reaching up to a high shelf.
Harder items include walking in a crowded mall and walking on an icy sidewalk.
Confidence for each activity is rated from 0 to 100 percent, and the average is taken.

cumleler.yazi: Unlike the DHI, on the ABC a high score means a better state and a low score a worse one.
cumleler.ses: Unlike the D H I, on the ABC a high score means a better state and a low score a worse one.

cumleler: In older adults, an ABC score below 67 percent is a commonly used cutoff linked to fall risk.
The scale also reveals activities avoided because of fear of falling.
The Turkish adaptation of the ABC scale has been studied both in older adults and in people with unilateral peripheral vestibular disease.
Low balance confidence can lead the person to avoid movement and, over time, to deconditioning.
So the ABC is useful for seeing fear of falling and setting rehabilitation goals.

cumleler.yazi: Used with the DHI, it gives a complementary picture: one shows perceived handicap, the other balance confidence.
cumleler.ses: Used with the D H I, it gives a complementary picture: one shows perceived handicap, the other balance confidence.

cumleler: Scale scores are interpreted together with performance tests such as the Timed Up and Go test or the Dynamic Gait Index.
There is a simple way to fit scales into the clinical workflow.
At the first assessment, the scale is completed and the baseline score is recorded.
Items with high scores show the areas the person struggles with most and the rehabilitation goals.
At set intervals, the same scale is completed again in the same way.
If the difference in scores is beyond measurement error, it is read as a meaningful change.
The same results can also be used to show the patient their progress in concrete terms.
There are other self-report scales for dizziness as well.
The Vertigo Symptom Scale asks about how often symptoms occur and about accompanying anxiety symptoms.
The Vestibular Disorders Activities of Daily Living Scale assesses independence in daily tasks.
For a quick assessment, a visual analog scale from 0 to 10 can also be used.
The choice of scale depends on the clinical question and on whether the scale has been validated in the patient's language.
Whichever scale is chosen, the same scale must always be used in follow-up.

sahneler.metin: Have the scale completed before vestibular testing. Nausea and fatigue after testing can affect answers; check that no item is left blank.
cumleler: A clinical tip: have the scale completed before vestibular testing, in the waiting room.
After testing, the patient may be nauseated and tired, which can shift the answers in a negative direction.
Check whether any item on the form is left blank; a missing item makes the total score look lower than it is.
In follow-up, having the scale completed under similar conditions each time makes comparison reliable.

maddeler.metin: ABC: balance confidence, high is good

cumleler.yazi: The DHI has 25 items grouped into three subscales and is scored from 0 to 100.
cumleler.ses: The D H I has 25 items grouped into three subscales and is scored from 0 to 100.

cumleler: For each item, yes scores 4, sometimes 2, and no 0; a higher score shows greater impact.
In follow-up, a difference of about 18 points is needed for a change to count as beyond measurement error.
The ABC scale measures balance confidence as a percentage; here a high score shows a better state.

sahneler.soru: How many points does sometimes score on the DHI?

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: on the Dizziness Handicap Inventory, how many points does a sometimes answer score?

cumleler: The correct answer is B: 2 points.
A yes answer scores 4 and a no answer scores 0, so across 25 items the total score ranges from 0 to 100.
